//: The pickers: one screen for each way a parameter of an action is asked for (12 §9.3). A profile names each for a role `picker.<name>`. Every picker may declare the parameters `title`, `action`, `param`, `value` and `options`, and answers with `answer`; Esc closes it, which abandons the whole command. The two below move a cursor over the map: the scene keeps the variables they declare up to date with what the party knows of the place under the cursor, and draws the line from the character to it.
title: Choose a place

text.value: <title>{$title ?? 'Choose a place'}</>  {if screen.cursor_sight == 'seen' then 'In sight' else if screen.cursor_sight == 'remembered' then 'Remembered' else 'Not known'}, {screen.cursor_distance:.1} m.{if screen.cursor_reach == 'yes' then ' In reach.' else if screen.cursor_reach == 'no' then ' Out of reach.' else ''} {screen.cursor_why} {screen.cursor_advice}
<dim>Direction keys move, Tab goes to the next thing, Enter chooses, Esc cancels.{if screen.picker_entries > 0 then ' Backspace takes a step back, Ctrl-D ends.' else ''}</>

//: The entity picker: the cursor starts on what the parameter is filled in with, or else on the nearest thing that could be chosen, and Tab cycles through the rest. Only what the party perceives can be chosen: Enter on an empty cell is refused.
title: Choose a target

text.value: <title>{$title ?? 'Choose a target'}</>  {if screen.cursor_target != '' then cap(screen.cursor_target) else 'Nobody there'} ({screen.cursor_index} of {screen.cursor_count}), {screen.cursor_distance:.1} m.{if screen.cursor_reach == 'yes' then ' In reach.' else if screen.cursor_reach == 'no' then ' Out of reach.' else ''} {screen.cursor_why} {screen.cursor_advice}
<dim>Tab goes to the next, direction keys move, Enter chooses, Esc cancels.</>

//: The direction picker: one key. It is in the `targeting` context, so the direction keys have their names, and each answers with the direction's word. An `act` asks for a parameter with it by saying so in `pick`, since a direction is a text like any other.
title: Which way?

text.value:
y k u
h . l
b j n
<dim>A direction key chooses; << and > are up and down.</>

//: The number picker. The scene fills `value` in with what the parameter is filled in with, whole for a whole number. Type a number and press Enter to take it, then Enter to accept; Left and Right step it.
title: How much?

rows.text: <dim>Type or step with Left and Right; Enter accepts.</>

//: The text picker, for a parameter that is a text with nothing to choose it from.
title: What?

//: The multi-pick, for a list parameter: Enter takes an entry or puts it back, and Done ends the list once it has at least its least count. The scene marks the entries that are in the list as `chosen` and keeps `picker_entries` at how many there are.
title: Choose several

list.empty: There is nothing to choose from.

rows.text: <dim>{screen.picker_entries} chosen. Enter takes or puts back.</>
<dim>{screen.picker_entries} of at most {$max} chosen. Enter takes or puts back.</>

//: The reaction prompt: what a decision of the kind `reaction` opens (the role `decision.reaction`). `what` says what is happening as the character perceives it (who does what); `options` is a list of maps with `label`, `value`, the option's number, and `late`, whether it would come too late; the bar is the time left of the window, in the character's own time. Choosing one answers with its number; Esc and the last button answer with nothing, which lets it happen. A reaction that must be told something opens a picker first.
title: React

rows.text: {cap(name($who))} can react, with {$time_left ?? 0:.1} s to spare.

list.empty: There is nothing to answer with.

//: The choice prompt: what a decision of the kind `choice` opens (the role `decision.choice`), put by a rule's `ask`. A choice must be made, so nothing here closes it.
title: Choose
